body:
## Summary

The lizard sanitizer and the parity check do not recognize a for-in loop over a function-literal table at file scope. `testkit/lizard_sighted.lua` passes that shape through unchanged, lizard 1.24.0 then crashes on it, and the runner cannot tell that crash apart from a blind file.

## Where (file:line)

- `testkit/lizard_sighted.lua:126-145`: the shadow and sanitize pass leaves the shape unchanged.
- The parity rows the runner reads (`testkit/run-automated-tests.sh:513`) have only one bucket, "blind". A file whose functions went unmeasured because lizard crashed lands in that same bucket.

## Repro

`for name, fn in pairs({ A = function() end }) do end` at file scope in any addon `.lua`. Run the complexity suite. lizard raises, and the file is reported as blind with no word on why.

## Proposed change

- Handle the shape in the runner: put `crashed` rows (lizard raised on this file, found by the per-file retry in the companion issue) in their own bucket, separate from `blind`.
- Optionally add an `S.forInFunctionLiterals(src)` detector, so the note can name the fix: "hoist the table to a local".
- Ship in the same release as the companion runner-exit-status issue: https://github.com/tusharsaxena/LibKa0s/issues/46

## Tests

Cases in `testkit/test_lizard_sighted.lua`: the detector finds the file-scope shape and does not fire on a hoisted local table. A runner fixture where a crashing file shows up as `crashed`, not `blind`.

## Found by

`PremadeGroupsFilterExtension docs/reviews/2026-10-10/06_CONSOLIDATED_FINDINGS.md` C-14 (the 2026-10-10 audit and review of Ka0s Premade Groups Filter Extension). The addon fixed its own instance locally by hoisting the table (C-02).

**Severity:** `low`, rated by impact. This is a tooling ergonomics defect in the shared kit and gives no wrong verdict once the companion issue lands. The "audit-carried deviation -> high" row does not apply. Re-rate it if you read the vocabulary differently.

title: Sanitizer/parity do not recognize the file-scope for-in function-literal shape
